text:
alex_m: quick sync — we need runtime + infra + console to agree on telemetry for per-route latency/throughput dashboards (P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec). who owns what and where do metrics get emitted?

maya: +1. main questions: where do we record TTFT (first token emitted) vs full request latency, and do we use histograms or summaries for Pxx? :eyes:

samuel: runtime should emit raw timers as histograms for request latency (bucketed) and an explicit TTFT timer. example metric names i propose (prom style):
```
redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="gpt-4o",route_id="r23",region="us-east-1",deployment="dedicated"} <value>
redwood_request_duration_seconds_sum/count
redwood_ttft_seconds_bucket{...}
redwood_tokens_emitted_total{model...,route_id...} <counter>
```
For tokens/sec i'd prefer we emit only a counter for tokens emitted and derive rate(...) in dashboards/alerts. emitting a gauge for tokens/sec from runtime is noisy.

samuel: TTFT definition: time from request accept (router receive) to first byte sent from runtime. runtime can record moment we flush first token to client. router should also annotate request with route_id/model so we keep labels low-cardinality.

javi: cardinality note — route_id must be a short stable id (not full URL or user id). console can map route_id -> human name. we shouldn't emit freeform tags like team_name or feature_name at high cardinality.

emily_r: for console dashboard UX: we want panels for per-route P50/P95/P99, TTFT P95, tokens/sec heatmap over time, and a per-model rollup. also a canary panel that shows canary vs baseline deltas. need to know which labels exist so we can wire filters (model, route_id, region, deployment).

jenna_prod: storage/cost constraints: raw histograms at full cardinality for 90k routes will explode. suggested compromise:
- emit histograms at runtime only for top-5k active routes (by traffic), sampled or aggregated elsewhere for the rest
- for low volume routes, emit timers as summary or capture percentiles in the runtime and send sampled summaries (or emit counts into coarse buckets)
- keep 7d of full-resolution histograms, 90d of rollups (per-model / per-region)
This requires a router-side sampler or a tagging rule.

maya: how about an API between runtime and metrics-collector: runtime attaches labels {route_id, model, deployment, instance_id, fallback=true/false}, and the collector handles sampling and aggregation rules. that keeps collectors flexible.

samuel: collector-side aggregation lgtm. runtime will emit: latency histogram, ttft histogram, tokens_emitted counter, request_success counter, request_retries counter. we'll include instance_id for debugging but mark it as high-cardinality and only keep for 7d.

emily_r: alerting thoughts:
- P95(latency) per-route > Xms for 5m -> page
- TTFT regressions on canary: if canary P95 TTFT >= baseline + 20% over 10m -> pager
- Drop in tokens/sec per-route -> paging for large routes only
We also want a dashboard panel for recent rollout windows showing delta bars.

javi: UI/ID mapping: we'll add a small metadata service that maps route_id -> {display_name, owner, product_area} so console can label dashboards without changing telemetry labels. route owners can update without touching runtime.

alex_m: concrete handoff checklist?

maya: proposed handoff items:
1) metric names + label set (runtime): redwood_request_duration_seconds (histogram), redwood_ttft_seconds (histogram), redwood_tokens_emitted_total (counter), redwood_requests_total (counter), redwood_request_errors_total (counter)
2) labels: model, route_id, region, deployment, fallback, quantized_instance (optional)
3) sampling rules (infra): collector config for top-N + sampled rest + retention policy
4) dashboard spec (console): list of panels, example queries, thresholds for alerts
5) mapping service (platform): route_id -> display metadata and route grouping
6) rollout/ canary test plan for validating metrics during deploys

samuel: here's a tiny Go pseudo snippet for runtime TTFT emit:
```go
start := time.Now()
// accept req...
firstTokenSent() {
  ttft := time.Since(start).Seconds()
  metrics.Histogram("redwood_ttft_seconds").Observe(ttft, labels)
}
finish() {
  metrics.Histogram("redwood_request_duration_seconds").Observe(time.Since(start).Seconds(), labels)
  metrics.Counter("redwood_tokens_emitted_total").Add(tokens)
}
```

jenna_prod: for sampling rule we can implement a fallback: if route traffic > 100qps -> full histograms. else if qps in [1,100) -> sampled 1/x requests where x = max(1, floor(100/qps)). else -> emit counters & coarse buckets. We'll add this to collector config.

emily_r: can console team get a sample dashboard json/schema so we can start building panels while infra lands sampling? saves time.

alex_m: actions:
- samuel + maya: finalize metric names & exact label list by EOD tomorrow (owner: samuel)
- jenna_prod: draft collector sampling config + retention proposal by Wed (owner: jenna_prod)
- javi + emily_r: mock dashboard layout + mapping API stub by Fri (owners: javi, emily_r)
- platform infra: create route_id mapping service ticket (owner: javi)

alex_m: thanks all. tagging @deploy-bot so we can test a small canary once metrics are wired. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: noted — will run canary once owners mark their tasks done (reacted :white_check_mark:).

(reacted :eyes: by maya)
